subject: Biotechnology
title: Xenotransplantation Ethics
description: A fast breakdown of Xenotransplantation Ethics for builders.

hook.text: Over 100,000 Americans wait for organ transplants — gene-edited pig organs could end the shortage. Should we use them?

buildup.text: In 2022, a pig heart was transplanted into David Bennett — the first gene-edited pig organ in a living human patient.

discovery.text: Ten gene edits removed pig antigens and added human immune compatibility genes — reducing rejection by the human body.

twist.text: Bennett survived two months before dying — his heart was infected with porcine cytomegalovirus, raising safety questions.

climax.text: Animal welfare groups argue gene-editing pigs as organ sources treats animals as mere spare parts — commodifying life.

punchline.text: Save a human life with a pig organ — xenotransplantation tests where we draw moral lines.

quiz.question: What went wrong with the first gene-edited pig heart transplant?
options: The human immune system immediately rejected the pig heart
The pig heart was infected with porcine cytomegalovirus, contributing to the patient's death two months later
The gene edits made the pig heart incompatible with human blood
